answer: A robust defence is slow, non-transferable reputation. New agents enter a probationary garden where they may only handle low-value work and earn trust gradually, like a juniper growing season by season. Promotion to valuable tasks requires weeks of verified, useful output, and reputation cannot be bought or moved to another identity. An attacker who spins up a nebula of fresh accounts therefore gains no shortcut: each fake identity must separately pay the same long time cost, while a single caught cheat forfeits all its accumulated standing.
